title: Frog 1
key_idea: Represent the minimum cost to reach stone i using optimal substructure from the previous two stones.
observation: At any stone i, the frog can only arrive from i-1 or i-2. The state space is linear O(N) and transitions depend only on local height differences |h_i - h_{i-k}|.
algorithm:
1. Initialize dp[1] = 0, dp[2] = |h_2 - h_1|.
2. For i from 3 to N: dp[i] = min(dp[i-1] + |h_i - h_{i-1}|, dp[i-2] + |h_i - h_{i-2}|).
3. Answer is dp[N].
complexity: Time: O(N), Space: O(N) or O(1) rolling state.
editorial_comparison: Directly matches canonical DP forward/backward relaxation.
teaches: Foundational DP state definition, base cases, and optimal substructure.
novel_value: Minimalist transition dependency and state compression.

title: Frog 2
key_idea: Generalize linear transitions to arbitrary step sizes K <= 100.
observation: Each dp[i] is computed by taking the minimum over the preceding K states: dp[i] = min_{1 <= j <= K} (dp[i-j] + |h_i - h_{i-j}|).
algorithm:
1. Set dp[1] = 0, all other dp[i] = INF.
2. Loop i from 1 to N-1; loop step j from 1 to K: relax dp[i+j] = min(dp[i+j], dp[i] + |h_{i+j} - h_i|).
3. Result is dp[N].
editorial_comparison: Matches push-based / pull-based relaxation over lookback window.
teaches: Parametric transition loops in DP and push-style vs pull-style relaxation.
novel_value: Transitions with variable bounds min(i+K, N).

title: Vacation
key_idea: Maintain happiness while enforcing non-repeating consecutive activity constraints.
observation: The valid choice on day i depends exclusively on the specific activity chosen on day i-1. Encoding the previous choice into the state resolves the constraint.
algorithm:
1. dp[i][act] = maximum happiness up to day i ending with activity act in {A, B, C}.
2. dp[i][A] = a_i + max(dp[i-1][B], dp[i-1][C]), and symmetrically for B and C.
3. Answer is max(dp[N][A], dp[N][B], dp[N][C]).
complexity: Time: O(N * 3), Space: O(3) using rolling variables.
teaches: State augmentation to satisfy Markovian transition constraints.
novel_value: Canonical state-machine DP with categorical transitions.

title: Knapsack 1
key_idea: Classical 0/1 Knapsack where capacity W <= 10^5 serves as the DP state index.
observation: Each item can be taken at most once. Traversing capacity downwards (from W down to w_i) prevents using the same item multiple times in 1D memory.
algorithm:
1. Initialize dp[0..W] = 0.
2. For each item (w_i, v_i): for w from W down to w_i: dp[w] = max(dp[w], dp[w - w_i] + v_i).
3. Answer is max(dp[0..W]).
teaches: 0/1 Knapsack state optimization and 1D space reduction technique.
novel_value: Reverse loop space compression.

title: Knapsack 2
topic: Knapsack Dual State / Value as State
key_idea: When weight capacity W is up to 10^9, invert the state: define dp[v] as the minimum weight required to achieve exact value v.
observation: N <= 100 and v_i <= 1000 implies total value V_max <= 10^5. The value dimension is small enough for pseudopolynomial DP, whereas weight is not.
algorithm:
1. Let V_sum = sum(v_i) <= 10^5. Set dp[0] = 0, dp[1..V_sum] = INF.
2. For each item (w_i, v_i): for v from V_sum down to v_i: dp[v] = min(dp[v], dp[v - v_i] + w_i).
3. Answer is max value v such that dp[v] <= W.
editorial_comparison: Classic state-inversion paradigm in competitive programming.
teaches: Dual problem formulation and state parameter swapping.
novel_value: Inverting objective and constraint when constraint space is too large.

title: LCS
key_idea: Find the actual string corresponding to the Longest Common Subsequence of s and t.
observation: Table dp[i][j] stores the length of LCS for prefixes s[1..i] and t[1..j]. Once filled, the actual string can be reconstructed by backtracking from (len(s), len(t)).
algorithm:
1. Fill standard LCS table: if s[i-1] == t[j-1]: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1; else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
2. Traceback: while i > 0 and j > 0: if s[i-1] == t[j-1], append char, i--, j--; else if dp[i-1][j] >= dp[i][j-1], i--; else j--.
3. Reverse reconstructed characters.
teaches: DP solution path reconstruction and parent/transition backtracking.
novel_value: Two-pointer matrix reconstruction of optimal decisions.

title: Longest Path
key_idea: Find the length of the longest directed path in a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG).
observation: Since the graph is acyclic, a topological ordering exists. The longest path starting at vertex u is dp[u] = 1 + max_{(u, v) in E} dp[v].
algorithm:
1. Compute out-degrees or use memoized DFS: memo[u] = -1.
2. DFS(u): if memo[u] != -1 return memo[u]. ans = 0. For each neighbor v of u: ans = max(ans, 1 + DFS(v)). memo[u] = ans.
3. Answer is max_{u in V} DFS(u).
complexity: Time: O(V + E), Space: O(V + E).
editorial_comparison: Equivalent to topological sort DP or memoized DFS.
teaches: Topological order as the fundamental validity condition for DAG DP.
novel_value: Connecting graph traversals directly to DP state transition graphs.

title: Grid 1
topic: Grid DP / Path Counting with Obstacles
key_idea: Count paths from top-left (1,1) to bottom-right (H,W) moving only right and down, avoiding walls.
observation: Number of ways to reach (r, c) is dp[r][c] = (dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1]) mod (10^9 + 7). If cell (r, c) is '#', dp[r][c] = 0.
algorithm:
1. dp[1][1] = 1.
2. For r from 1 to H: for c from 1 to W: if grid[r][c] == '#': dp[r][c] = 0; else add dp[r-1][c] and dp[r][c-1] mod 10^9+7.
3. Output dp[H][W].
complexity: Time: O(H * W), Space: O(W) rolling array.
teaches: Modular arithmetic integration into DP transitions and grid boundary conditions.
novel_value: Translating geometric movement constraints into 2D recurrences.

title: Coins
key_idea: Calculate the probability that more heads than tails appear when tossing N biased coins.
observation: Let dp[i][j] be the probability of having exactly j heads after tossing the first i coins. dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] * p_i + dp[i-1][j] * (1 - p_i).
algorithm:
1. dp[0][0] = 1.0; all others 0.0.
2. For i from 1 to N: for j from 0 to i: dp[i][j] = (j > 0 ? dp[i-1][j-1] * p_i : 0) + dp[i-1][j] * (1 - p_i).
3. Sum dp[N][j] for all j > N / 2.
teaches: Probability DP state independence and floating-point stability.
novel_value: Discrete event convolution over independent trials.

title: Stones
key_idea: Determine whether First or Second player wins an impartial subtract-a-stone game from pile of size K.
observation: A state x is a Winning state (First wins) if there exists a valid move a_i <= x such that x - a_i is a Losing state (Second wins). If all valid moves lead to Winning states, x is Losing.
algorithm:
1. dp[0] = False (Losing state).
2. For x from 1 to K: dp[x] = True if any(a_i <= x and not dp[x - a_i] for a_i in A) else False.
3. Output 'First' if dp[K] else 'Second'.
editorial_comparison: Classic backward induction on finite game graph.
teaches: Backward induction, P-positions and N-positions, and impartial game theory.
novel_value: Boolean state alternation under optimal play.

title: Deque
topic: Interval DP / Range DP / Matrix Chain Multiplication (MCM)
key_idea: Two players take turns removing elements from either end of a deque. Maximize X - Y.
observation: For subsegment [l, r], the active player chooses either a_l or a_r to maximize their margin over the remaining subsegment: dp[l][r] = max(a_l - dp[l+1][r], a_r - dp[l][r-1]).
algorithm:
1. Base case: for i in 1..N: dp[i][i] = a_i.
2. Iterate interval length len from 2 to N: for l from 1 to N - len + 1: r = l + len - 1: dp[l][r] = max(a_l - dp[l+1][r], a_r - dp[l][r-1]).
3. Answer is dp[1][N].
teaches: Interval DP structure (solving by increasing segment length) and minimax evaluation.
novel_value: Symmetric negation optimization in zero-sum sequential games.

title: Candies
key_idea: Distribute K candies among N children such that child i receives at most a_i candies.
observation: Direct transition dp[i][j] = sum_{k=0}^{min(j, a_i)} dp[i-1][j-k] takes O(N * K^2). The inner sum is over a contiguous range [j - a_i, j] in dp[i-1], which prefix sums evaluate in O(1).
algorithm:
1. dp[0] = 1, all others 0.
2. For each child i: compute prefix sums pref of current dp: pref[x+1] = (pref[x] + dp[x]) mod M.
3. New dp[j] = (pref[j+1] - pref[max(0, j - a_i)]) mod M.
4. Answer is dp[K].
editorial_comparison: Prefix sum acceleration of polynomial transitions.
teaches: Transition acceleration from O(K) to O(1) via prefix sums on DP states.
novel_value: Sliding window range-sum transition optimization.

title: Slimes
topic: Interval DP / Range DP / Matrix Chain Multiplication (MCM)
key_idea: Merge N slimes pairwise into one slime with minimum total combining cost.
observation: The final merge combines two sub-blocks [l, k] and [k+1, r]. The cost incurred at the final step is sum_{i=l}^r a_i. dp[l][r] = sum(a[l..r]) + min_{l <= k < r} (dp[l][k] + dp[k+1][r]).
algorithm:
1. Precompute prefix sums of array a.
2. dp[i][i] = 0.
3. Loop length len from 2 to N: loop left l from 1 to N-len+1: r = l+len-1: dp[l][r] = min_{k=l}^{r-1}(dp[l][k] + dp[k+1][r]) + (pref[r] - pref[l-1]).
4. Output dp[1][N].
complexity: Time: O(N^3) standard, reducible to O(N^2) via Knuth's Optimization.
editorial_comparison: Direct equivalent to Matrix Chain Multiplication / optimal binary search tree.
teaches: Interval merging DP and partition point split optimization.
novel_value: Prefix sum cost addition over nested subproblem partitions.

title: Matching
key_idea: Count the number of perfect matchings in a bipartite graph with N men and N women (N <= 21).
observation: When matching men 0, 1, ..., i-1, the number of matched women is exactly i = popcount(mask). Hence the man's index is implicit in the bitmask of chosen women!
algorithm:
1. dp[0] = 1, all other dp[mask] = 0.
2. For mask from 0 to 2^N - 1: let i = popcount(mask). If i == N, continue.
3. For each woman j in 0..N-1: if not (mask & (1 << j)) and compatible(i, j): dp[mask | (1 << j)] = (dp[mask | (1 << j)] + dp[mask]) mod (10^9 + 7).
4. Answer is dp[(1 << N) - 1].
teaches: Dimension reduction in Bitmask DP using state invariants (popcount).
novel_value: Implicit step derivation from subset cardinality.

title: Independent Set
key_idea: Count ways to paint vertices of a tree black or white such that no two adjacent vertices are both black.
observation: Root the tree arbitrarily. For any node u, if u is painted Black, all children must be White. If u is painted White, each child can be either Black or White independently.
algorithm:
1. Post-order DFS(u, parent).
2. dp[u][Black] = prod_{v in children(u)} dp[v][White].
3. dp[u][White] = prod_{v in children(u)} (dp[v][Black] + dp[v][White]).
4. Return (dp[root][Black] + dp[root][White]) mod 10^9+7.
teaches: Subtree DP, state-color branching, and product-rule combination over tree children.
novel_value: Independent combination of child subtree configurations.

title: Flowers
topic: DP Optimization using Data Structures [Some Practice Problems]
key_idea: Find a subsequence of flowers with strictly increasing heights that maximizes total beauty.
observation: Let dp[h] be the maximum beauty of an increasing subsequence ending at height h. For a flower with height h_i and beauty a_i, dp[h_i] = a_i + max_{0 <= h < h_i} dp[h]. This requires dynamic point update and prefix maximum query.
algorithm:
1. Maintain a Fenwick tree (or Segment Tree) of size N storing max DP values.
2. For each flower i from 1 to N: best = query_prefix_max(h_i - 1); val = best + a_i; point_update(h_i, val).
3. Answer is query_prefix_max(N).
complexity: Time: O(N log N), Space: O(N).
teaches: Accelerating O(N^2) DP to O(N log N) using Fenwick/Segment Tree on value domain.
novel_value: Transforming inner range search into dynamic range queries.

title: Grouping
key_idea: Partition N rabbits into groups to maximize total compatibility score (N <= 16).
observation: Precompute the score of any standalone group submask in O(N^2 * 2^N). Then dp[mask] = max_{sub is submask of mask} (cost[sub] + dp[mask ^ sub]).
algorithm:
1. Precompute cost[mask] for all 2^N masks.
2. Loop mask from 1 to 2^N - 1:
   Iterate submasks: sub = mask; while sub > 0: dp[mask] = max(dp[mask], cost[sub] + dp[mask ^ sub]); sub = (sub - 1) & mask.
3. Total submask transitions over all masks sum to 3^N.
teaches: O(3^N) submask iteration idiom and subset partition DP.
novel_value: The (sub - 1) & mask bit trick for exhaustive partition.

title: Subtree
key_idea: For every node v in a tree, compute the number of black-connected components containing v modulo M.
observation: Recomputing tree DP for each root takes O(N^2). Since M is not necessarily prime, modular division is forbidden! Prefix and suffix products of children's answers allow O(1) rerooting without division.
algorithm:
1. Post-order DFS1: compute subtree product down[u] = prod_{v in children} (down[v] + 1) mod M.
2. Pre-order DFS2: compute parent contribution up[u] using prefix and suffix products of sibling values (down[sib] + 1).
3. Final answer for u: down[u] * (up[u] + 1) mod M.
editorial_comparison: All-roots tree DP rerooting with non-invertible operators.
teaches: Tree rerooting technique without division using prefix/suffix product arrays.
novel_value: Rerooting under arbitrary modulus without modular inverses.

title: Frog 3
topic: Convex Hull Trick (CHT) and Dynamic CHT
key_idea: Frog jumps from stone i to j with cost (h_j - h_i)^2 + C.
observation: Expanding (h_j - h_i)^2 + C yields h_j^2 + C + (h_i^2 + dp[i]) - 2 * h_j * h_i. For fixed j, this is min_i { m_i * x + b_i } where m_i = -2 * h_i and b_i = h_i^2 + dp[i]. Since heights h_i are strictly increasing, lines have monotonically decreasing slopes!
algorithm:
1. Maintain a Convex Hull of lines in a deque.
2. Query optimal line for x = h_j by popping suboptimal lines from the front.
3. Compute dp[j].
4. Add new line (slope = -2*h_j, intercept = h_j^2 + dp[j]) to back, popping non-convex lines.
complexity: Time: O(N) amortized with monotone deque (or O(N log N) via Li Chao Tree).
editorial_comparison: Canonical Convex Hull Trick with monotonic slopes and monotonic queries.
teaches: CHT line representation, geometric lower envelope maintenance, and linear time DP optimization.
novel_value: Linear-time optimization of quadratic transition costs.

title: New Friends
topic: Disjoint Set Union (DSU) / Connected Component Cliques
key_idea: If A-B and B-C are friends, A and C can become friends. Count maximum new operations.
observation: The friendship relation is transitive under repeated operations. Thus, each connected component of size S will eventually become a complete graph (clique) with S*(S-1)/2 edges.
algorithm:
1. Build Disjoint Set Union (DSU) over all N vertices and M edges.
2. For each component root, obtain component size S and count existing edges E.
3. Total new edges = sum_{components} (S * (S - 1) / 2 - E).
complexity: Time: O(N + M * alpha(N)), Space: O(N).
teaches: Transitive closure on undirected graphs and component-wise clique completion.
novel_value: Translating local operation chains into global component invariants.

title: Yokan Party
topic: Binary Search on Answer / Greedy Feasibility
key_idea: Cut a stick of length L at K positions to maximize the minimum piece length.
observation: Maximizing the minimum of something is the hallmark signature of Binary Search on Answer. The predicate 'Can we obtain at least K+1 pieces of length >= M?' is monotonic in M.
algorithm:
1. Binary search for M in [1, L].
2. Feasibility check check(M): Greedily cut whenever the accumulated piece length reaches >= M. If total pieces cut is >= K and remaining piece is >= M, return True; else False.
3. High boundary of binary search gives the maximum possible minimum length.
complexity: Time: O(N log L), Space: O(1).
teaches: Binary search on answer and greedy feasibility check.
novel_value: The canonical 'maximize the minimum' CP template.

title: Longest Circular Road
key_idea: Adding an edge between two vertices u and v creates a cycle of length dist(u, v) + 1. Maximize this cycle length.
observation: Maximizing dist(u, v) in a tree is precisely finding the diameter of the tree! The maximum cycle length is diameter + 1.
algorithm:
1. Run BFS from arbitrary node (e.g. node 1) to find the farthest node u.
2. Run BFS from node u to find the farthest node v. The distance dist(u, v) is the tree diameter.
3. Output dist(u, v) + 1.
teaches: Tree diameter characterization and the 2-BFS proof.
novel_value: Connecting cycle maximization to tree diameter.

title: Red Painting
key_idea: Dynamically color grid cells red and answer reachability queries between red cells.
observation: When a cell (r, c) is colored red, it unites with any adjacent red neighbors. Querying if two red cells are connected is equivalent to checking if they belong to the same DSU set.
algorithm:
1. Map 2D grid coordinates (r, c) to 1D index r * W + c.
2. Initialize DSU and boolean grid is_red.
3. Query 1: Mark (r, c) red; for each neighbor (nr, nc) that is red, dsu.unite(idx(r,c), idx(nr,nc)).
4. Query 2: If both cells are red and dsu.same(idx(ra,ca), idx(rb,cb)), print 'Yes', else 'No'.
complexity: Time: O(Q * alpha(H * W)), Space: O(H * W).
teaches: 2D-to-1D index linearization and online grid connectivity.
novel_value: Online union-find query handling without rebuilding components.

title: Past ABCs
key_idea: Check if a string matches ABC001 to ABC349 excluding ABC316.
observation: Pure statement simulation. Extract integer suffix, check 1 <= num <= 349 and num != 316.
algorithm: Parse substring [3:6] into integer, test conditions.
teaches: Basic syntax, string slicing, and conditional branching.
novel_value: None. Low transferable value for competitive programming algorithms.
rejection_reason: REJECTED: Basic logic building / syntax simulation. Lacks reusable algorithmic paradigm.

title: Dentist Aoki
key_idea: Toggle tooth state between present and absent across Q queries.
observation: Maintain boolean array of size N. For each query T_i, invert tooth[T_i]. Count True entries.
algorithm: Array indexing and boolean negation.
editorial_comparison: Direct simulation with boolean array or set.
teaches: Elementary array indexing and counting.
novel_value: None. Elementary simulation.
rejection_reason: REJECTED: Routine logic building / array simulation without generalizable data structures.

title: Product
key_idea: Determine whether product a * b is even or odd.
observation: Product is odd if and only if both a and b are odd.
algorithm: Check (a * b) % 2 == 1.
teaches: Arithmetic operators and modulo.
novel_value: None.
rejection_reason: REJECTED: Intro beginner logic building; no algorithmic relevance.

title: Placing Marbles
key_idea: Count occurrences of character '1' in a 3-character string.
observation: Count matching characters.
algorithm: string.count('1').
teaches: String traversal.
novel_value: None.
rejection_reason: REJECTED: Intro syntax exercise without reusable algorithmic depth.
